title: Cognitive Bias Observatory methodology
scope: A transparent headline-level measurement layer for cognitive-pressure signals in public information environments. It does not diagnose authors, audiences or outlets with cognitive biases.
unitOfAnalysis: One headline plus source metadata. Article bodies are not copied or analyzed in v0.1.
interpretationRule: Report observable lexical and structural signals. Do not infer a cognitive bias, intent, truthfulness, political position or causal effect from one signal.
samplingRule: Every snapshot must state its provider, query, date window, language, sample size and sampling limitations. Curated pilot snapshots must never be presented as representative media samples.

signals.label: Gain framing cue
signals.description: Counts words that foreground opportunity, growth, improvement or creation.

signals.label: Loss framing cue
signals.description: Counts words that foreground losses, cuts, decline, threat or damage.

signals.label: Uncertainty cue
signals.description: Counts modal or questioning language that keeps a claim open rather than presenting it as settled.

signals.label: Certainty cue
signals.description: Counts language that presents an outcome or relationship with stronger certainty.

signals.label: Salience cue
signals.description: Counts vivid or high-intensity words that can make a headline more attention-grabbing.

signals.label: Authority cue
signals.description: Counts references that foreground institutions, experts, studies, reports or named authority statements.

signals.label: Social proof cue
signals.description: Counts language emphasizing popularity, majorities, widespread behavior or crowd adoption.

signals.label: Numerical emphasis
signals.description: Counts explicit numerals, percentages, currencies and number-like tokens in the headline.
signals.rule: Regex-based count; no claim is made about whether the number is accurate or misleading.

signals.label: Question headline
signals.description: Marks headlines ending in a question mark. A question can signal uncertainty, curiosity or rhetorical framing, but the observable fact is only the form.

signals.label: Near-duplicate repetition
signals.description: Groups headlines that share a high proportion of content words after stop-word removal.
signals.rule: Pairwise Jaccard similarity >= 0.62. This detects similar wording, not shared truth or independent confirmation.

derivedViews.frameDirection: gain-leaning when gain cues exceed loss cues; loss-leaning when loss cues exceed gain cues; mixed-or-neutral when tied.
derivedViews.certaintyDirection: certainty-leaning when certainty cues exceed uncertainty cues; uncertainty-leaning when uncertainty cues exceed certainty cues; mixed-or-neutral when tied.
derivedViews.sourceDiversity: unique domains divided by record count. This is a sample property, not a quality score.
derivedViews.countryDiversity: unique non-empty source countries divided by record count.
